glosses: An institution where one can place and borrow money and take care of financial affairs.

examples.text: Finance is seldom romantic. But the idea of peer-to-peer lending comes close. This is an industry that brings together individual savers and lenders on online platforms.[…]Banks and credit-card firms are kept out of the picture. Talk to enough people in the field and someone is bound to mention the “democratisation of finance”.

glosses: A branch office of such an institution.
An underwriter or controller of a card game.
A fund from deposits or contributions, to be used in transacting business; a joint stock or capital.

examples.text: Let it be no bank or common stock, but every man be master of his own money.

glosses: The sum of money etc. which the dealer or banker has as a fund from which to draw stakes and pay losses.
Money; profit.

examples.text: Military dude was working for a drug dealer, right? and making good bank with it—he was making good money.

glosses: In certain games, such as dominos, a fund of pieces from which the players are allowed to draw.
A safe and guaranteed place of storage for and retrieval of important items or goods.

examples.text: blood bank; data bank; sperm bank

glosses: A device used to store coins or currency.

examples.text: If you want to buy a bicycle, you need to put the money in your piggy bank.

glosses: To deal with a bank or financial institution, or for an institution to provide financial services to a client.

examples.text: He banked with Barclays.
the sort of face you would happily bank with

glosses: To put into a bank.

examples.text: I’m going to bank the money.

glosses: To conceal in the rectum for use in prison.

examples.text: Johnny banked some coke for me.

glosses: To provide banking services to.

examples.text: They proposed an ambitious plan to bank people in remote rural communities.
For quotations using this term, see Citations:bank.

glosses: An edge of river, lake, or other watercourse.

examples.text: Tiber trembled underneath her banks.
On the opposite bank of the river other Chinese units attacked Taoshih and Yunmeng north-west of Hankow.
Just upstream of Dryburgh Abbey, a reproduction of a classical Greek temple stands at the top of a wooded hillock on the river’s north bank.

glosses: An elevation under the sea; a shallow area of shifting sand, gravel, mud, and so forth

examples.text: the banks of Newfoundland

glosses: A slope of earth, sand, etc.; an embankment.
The incline of an aircraft, especially during a turn.
An incline, a hill.

examples.text: This is the hardest duty on the railway, for the trains are heavy and there are some long 1 in 40 banks.

glosses: A mass of clouds.

examples.text: The bank of clouds on the horizon announced the arrival of the predicted storm front.

glosses: The face of the coal at which miners are working.
A deposit of ore or coal, worked by excavations above water level.
The ground at the top of a shaft.

examples.text: Ores are brought to bank.

glosses: To roll or incline laterally in order to turn.
To cause (an aircraft) to bank.
To form into a bank or heap, to bank up.

examples.text: to bank sand

glosses: To form a bank; to gather in masses.

examples.text: […] clouds banking above the gravel road, their flat slate-blue bottoms threatening freezing rain or an early snowfall.

glosses: To cover the embers of a fire with ashes in order to retain heat.
To raise a mound or dike about; to enclose, defend, or fortify with a bank; to embank.

examples.text: Aristoma∣chus would haue them to be stript from their leaues in winter, & in any hand to be banked well about, that the water stand not there in any hollow furrow or hole lower than the other ground

glosses: To pass by the banks of.

examples.text: Have I not heard these islanders shout out / Vive le roi! as I have banked their towns?

glosses: To provide additional power for a train ascending a bank (incline) by attaching another locomotive.

examples.text: Some interesting facts have recently been made known by the L.N.E.R. concerning the 178-ton Garratt 2-8-0 + 0-8-2 engine No. 2395, which since construction in 1925 has spent the whole of its working life banking coal trains up the 3 miles of 1 in 40 between Wentworth junction and West Silkstone, on the Worsborough branch, near Barnsley.
[...] the 4-4-0 unhappily stalled after a stop on Reading Old Bank with its eight-coach load and the Reading Up Line pilot, a "Hall", had to bank the train into Reading General.
Soon after leaving Bebra the line rises, mostly at 1 in 74, for 7 miles to Cornberg and all trains of over 400 tons are banked.

glosses: A row or panel of items stored or grouped together.

examples.text: a bank of switches
a bank of pay phones
Wanderers were finally woken from their slumber when Kevin Davies brought a fine save out of Brad Guzan while, minutes after the restart, Klasnic was blocked out by a bank of Villa defenders.

glosses: A row of keys on a musical keyboard or the equivalent on a typewriter keyboard.
A contiguous block of memory that is of fixed, hardware-dependent size, but often larger than a page and partitioning the memory such that two distinct banks do not overlap.
A set of multiple adjacent drop targets.
To arrange or order in a row.
A bench, as for rowers in a galley; also, a tier of oars.

examples.text: Placed on their banks, the lusty Trojans sweep / Neptune's smooth face, and cleave the yielding deep.

glosses: A bench or seat for judges in court.
The regular term of a court of law, or the full court sitting to hear arguments upon questions of law, as distinguished from a sitting at nisi prius, or a court held for jury trials. See banc
A kind of table used by printers.
A bench, or row of keys belonging to a keyboard, as in an organ.
